card.title: The labelled animal cell examiners expect

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Each organelle is a compartment that lets incompatible chemistry run at the same time, and a labelled drawing is how the paper asks you to prove you know them.

figure.caption: Labelled animal cell with membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, rough ER, mitochondrion, Golgi body and cytoplasm.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: RBC 7.5 μm;  membrane 7.5 nm trilaminar;  mitochondrion 1–10 μm;  ribosome 15–20 nm;  light-microscope limit 0.2 μm

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Draw only what that magnification can resolve — a light microscope cannot show ribosomes or the bilayer, so a drawing must not pretend to.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A mature human RBC has neither nucleus nor mitochondria; a plant cell adds a cell wall, a large central vacuole and plastids.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Full-mark answer: name the part, then give its function — membrane: the selective barrier; nucleus: stores the DNA and controls the cell's activity; mitochondrion: aerobic respiration releasing ATP; ribosome: protein synthesis; Golgi body: packaging and secretion of proteins.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: A diagram alone earns nothing: every label needs its function on its own line, and leader lines must not cross each other.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: The organelle model is testable: mitochondria carry their own DNA and 70S ribosomes behind a double membrane, the signature of an engulfed bacterium (endosymbiotic theory).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Draw the outline last and the organelles first, then give every label one function on a single line — tick marks follow labels and functions separately.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Draw a fully labelled diagram of an animal cell and give the function of any five labelled parts.
